brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
One of the two most common kinds of Lady Grey: Earl Grey tea combined with Seville oranges.

Recipes for a flavoured or scented tea vary from one maker to the next, so read the ingredient list and brew it like its base tea.
history: Lady Grey is a Twinings trademark. Little more is documented about this version.
processing: A black base tea flavoured or scented by the maker; the recipe varies.
harvest_season: The base tea can come from any picking, so the season matters less than the recipe.
appearance_dry: Usually dark twisted leaf, sometimes with golden tips.
taste_profile: Expect what black teas usually give: malty, sweet and brisk.
vintage_note: Flavoured and scented teas are not sold by vintage. Buy recent stock and drink it within a year or so, since the aroma fades.
